text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Sunday as reported by the official Algerian news agency APS. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government ministers pursue campaign across the country to draw support for November 28 referendum to change the constitution.
- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia tells expatriates' gathering in Rome the draft constitution will strengthen Algeria's institutional structure.
- The United States adjusts its position towards Algeria by condemning "terrorism" and encouraging investment in the country.
- Legal Islamist parties, Hamas and Nahda, call for participation in the referendum but give their supporters no order whether to vote for or against the proposed changes.
- University teachers decide to pursue strike and withdraw confidence in their union leader who want to suspend the action.
- A Bulgarian national killed in Algiers.
- Most of the suspected militants accused of murdering former prime minister Kasdi Merbah were released.
